effect.description: one run a commit owes, written in the commit's own transaction and claimed by whichever process runs it

handler.description: the declared effect it runs, by name

target.description: the entity the committed change was about

kind.description: what happened to it, or `matched` where a query matched it

state.description: how far the run got — pending until a worker settles it

attempts.description: how many times the handler has been started

generation.description: how deep in effect-written batches the commit that owed it was: 0 for a client's write, 1 for an effect's own, so what this run writes is one more

error.description: what the last attempt threw — kept beside a run left failed, so the record shows why

next.description: when the next attempt falls due; set means a failure that reported and is waiting out its backoff, absent means a run nobody has started or one in progress

lease_owner.description: the process that claimed this run

lease_token.description: that claim's token, fresh on every claim

lease_expiry.description: when the claim expires and another process may take it

lease.description: a duty held by one process at a time — its eid is derived from `name`, so two processes reaching for the same duty address one row and the winner is settled by the graph's own precondition

name.description: the duty being held — a sweep, a clock, a start-up pass; the eid is derived from it, so the same duty is the same row in every graph

holder.description: the process running it — absent means nobody is, and the next process to ask gets it

until.description: when the hold expires; a holder still working pushes this out on a timer, and one that was killed leaves a row that expires without anything having to clean up after it

provisional.description: an entity whose asynchronous step has not finished yet: it sits where it always does, and the effect that finishes the step removes this mark. A reader who sees it knows the entity is not settled; the writer who started the step waits for it and never sees the mark

note.description: a line for the person reading it: why the entity is provisional, such as "saving the key"

effect_check.title: Check effect runs
effect_check.description: Check recorded background actions (effects), such as sending mail after a transaction commits. Reports runs marked failed after exhausting their attempts, and runs still pending past their due time by more than the server’s threshold (10 minutes by default). An overdue run can indicate that no process is running them, even while graph writes succeed. Does not retry or mark runs failed itself; with no effect records supported by the schema, reports no findings. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.
